title: U.S. House · Illinois's 9th District
area: Chicago's North Side and North Shore suburbs, including Evanston, Skokie, Rogers Park and Glenview.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Jan Schakowsky did not run for re-election. Daniel K. Biss, the mayor of Evanston, won a crowded March 17, 2026 Democratic primary with 29.4% of the vote over Kat Abughazaleh (26.3%), Laura Fine (20.0%) and twelve other candidates. John Elleson won the Republican primary. Ballotpedia calculated the district's Cook Partisan Voter Index as D+19, based on the 2020 and 2024 presidential elections.

candidates.name: Daniel K. Biss
candidates.currentRole: Mayor of Evanston (since 2021; announced he would resign Oct. 18, 2026)

priorities.text: Says he has a record of passing legislation preserving access to abortion, changing campaign finance law, and setting stricter carbon-efficiency standards for buildings while in the state legislature and as mayor.
priorities.quote: a proven record of not just fighting the important fights, but winning

priorities.text: Says he would stand up to President Trump on immigration, preserving access to abortion, and expanding mental health services.
priorities.quote: stand up to Donald Trump on immigration, preserving access to abortion, expanding mental health services, and more

positions.summary: Says he has passed legislation preserving access to abortion and would continue to stand up for it in Congress.
Campaign site calls for universal background checks, a federal assault weapons ban, red flag laws and safe storage requirements.
positions.quote: Universal Background Checks: No loopholes, no exceptions.

positions.summary: Campaign site supports Medicare for All and reversing Medicaid and ACA premium support cuts.
positions.quote: We need to pass Medicare for All and deliver the affordable health care people enjoy in nearly every other advanced democracy.

positions.summary: Campaign site calls for a wealth tax on billionaires, rolling back Trump tax cuts for top earners, and raising the corporate tax rate.
positions.quote: We should implement a modest wealth tax on the assets of billionaires and ultra-millionaires to fund the priorities we all care about.

positions.summary: Campaign site calls for ending the Trump tariffs, describing them as a tax on working people.
positions.quote: we should get rid of Trump’s ridiculous tariffs, which are simply a tax on working people

positions.summary: Campaign site says he would work to sunset existing military authorizations and require congressional approval for future military actions.
positions.quote: require congressional approval for future military actions

record.text: Chaired the Illinois Senate Human Services Committee in the 2015 legislative session and the Labor Committee in the 2017 session.

priorities.text: Says he supports practical, aid-based programs for addiction, homelessness and mental health, and community-first healthcare policies expanding local clinics.
Says he would support law enforcement with resources and de-escalation training while focusing on keeping drugs off the streets.
Says he supports policies that uplift working families while protecting religious liberty, and removing burdensome business regulations.

positions.summary: Says he supports resourcing and training law enforcement, focused on de-escalation and community trust.
positions.quote: supporting law enforcement with resources and training rooted in de-escalation and community trust

statements.quote: We need bi-partisan legislation where some are going to get amnesty and some will have to go back to their home country.
statements.context: In his WTTW 2026 voter guide answers

statements.quote: We need bi-partisan legislation that helps the middle class afford health insurance. The poor need it, the elderly need it, the disabled need it.
statements.context: In his WTTW 2026 voter guide answers

statements.quote: Everyone should contribute something, but the higher earners need to pay their fair share.
statements.context: In his WTTW 2026 voter guide answers

researchNotes: Biss has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his key messages are drawn from a campaign advertisement and campaign website as summarized by Ballotpedia staff. John Elleson's statements come from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and WTTW 2026 voter-guide answers; his answers do not directly take a side on most guide issues. Biography gaps: Elleson's pastorate and degree year come from BallotReady, and no campaign site or news profile of his 2026 run was found; Biss's mayoral resignation (announced for Oct. 18, 2026) was reported by local media but not confirmed as completed.
